one_line_contribution: Replace per-instance top-k retrieval in procedural agent memory with the k most-frequently-retrieved items held fixed and verbatim for every query (the A_fix arm), and claim that mean pairwise top-k Jaccard overlap O, computable from the retriever with zero rollouts, predicts out of sample how much end-to-end accuracy that swap costs.
closest_prior_work: The proposal correctly names arXiv:2511.21730 as a partial collision on direction, but the work that most threatens novelty is one it never engages: the in-context demonstration-selection literature, where 'retrieved demonstrations vs a fixed/random demonstration set costs little' is a long-standing and repeatedly replicated finding on exactly the demonstration slot this track is framed around. Related Work item (7) pre-empts only the RAG-vs-long-context parallel and treats the objection as being about corpora; the demo-selection line is about k retrieved exemplars in a prompt, which is structurally identical to A_ret vs A_fix, and its known answer (fixed exemplars are usually within noise of retrieved ones on homogeneous task distributions) is the proposal's Prediction 1. Also unengaged: adaptive-retrieval / retrieval-necessity work in RAG, which already builds predictors of whether retrieval will pay, weakening the 'first pre-deployment diagnostic' framing to 'first corpus-level diagnostic for procedural banks'. Combined with the author's own concession that 2602.02751 scoops bank-size saturation outright and 2511.21730 establishes the direction, what is left as new is one statistic and one MMR cell.
strongest_objection: The headline law is close to an analytic identity, and the proposal never states the null that would show otherwise. O is defined as the mean pairwise Jaccard of the top-k sets, and A_fix injects (approximately) the modal top-k set; so O is a direct measure of how much of A_ret's prompt A_fix already reproduces. At O near 1.0 the two arms literally inject the same k items for nearly every test instance, so R_fix must be ~0 by construction, not by discovery; at O near 0 they share almost nothing. Prediction 2's 'leave-one-cell-out prediction of R_fix from O beats a grand mean' is therefore largely the statement that two conditions differ more in accuracy when they differ more in content, and the fitted 'crossing threshold' shipped as the deliverable inherits that. The proposal offers no analytic baseline (e.g. expected R_fix under a pure content-difference model scaling with (1-O) times the measured marginal per-item effect) against which the fit could be shown to carry information beyond the identity. Two reinforcing problems: (a) O is collinear with the very knobs used to move it - Jaccard falls mechanically as N grows and its scale is not comparable across k in {1,3,7} (at k=1 pairwise Jaccard is binary and reduces to modal-item frequency), so a 20-cell regression that pools cells differing simultaneously in environment, bank, N, retriever and k cannot separate O from 'which cell this is', and only two contrasts (dense vs MMR, E2-narrow vs E2-broad) vary diversity at fixed everything else; (b) with no retrieval upper bound in the design, a null R_fix cannot distinguish 'no per-instance information exists in this bank' from 'dense embedding retrieval over strategy-level items cannot find it' - which is precisely what the proposal's own cited ally 2511.21730 already demonstrated ('embeddings fundamentally treat procedures as unordered bags of words'). Under that reading the correct conclusion is 'fix the retriever', not 'the retriever is decorative', and the paper's title claim collapses. Secondary but concrete: Predictions 1 and 6 sit in tension - if MMR recovers >=3 points over dense at the same bank and k=7 in an O>0.5 cell while A_fix ties dense within 2 points, then a per-instance retrieval variant beats the frozen arm, which is the opposite of decorative, and no diversified-frozen-subset arm exists to resolve it. And the power arithmetic does not support Prediction 1: TOST needs more power than NHST, the stated single-cell MDEs are 4 (n=600), 6 (n=300) and 8-9 (E2 n=140/100), and by my count only about six of the roughly eleven high-overlap R_fix cells run at n=600, so 'per-cell TOST equivalence at a 4-point margin passes in >=8 of ~11 cells' is close to arithmetically unreachable as designed.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Publish the analytic null for the law: predict R_fix from (1-O) times the measured marginal effect of swapping one injected item, and require the O-fit to beat that, not just a grand mean - otherwise the diagnostic is a restatement of prompt distance. 2) Add at least three cells where O is moved with environment, bank, N and k all held fixed (retrieval temperature, embedding model, MMR lambda sweep); a law identified only across heterogeneous cells is not identified. 3) Normalize O against its random-set expectation so cells at k=1, 3 and 7 are on a comparable axis, and pre-register that normalized statistic rather than raw Jaccard. 4) Add a retrieval ceiling (oracle or task-type-labelled selection) so a null separates 'no instance-specific signal' from 'weak retriever'. 5) Add A_fix-MMR (diversity-selected frozen subset) so Prediction 6's MMR gain can be attributed to redundancy removal rather than to per-instance conditioning; without it Predictions 1 and 6 cannot both be reported as supporting the thesis. 6) Restate Prediction 1 as the random-effects meta-estimate only, and drop or re-power the per-cell TOST count, which the stated MDEs cannot deliver. 7) Either reproduce ReasoningBank's setup or demote claim (iii) from 'reinterprets their k-curve' to 'makes a compatible prediction in our setup' - the current wording promises a reinterpretation of numbers obtained on a different scaffold, models and benchmark.
missing_baseline: A mismatched-retrieval arm: per-instance top-k retrieval driven by a different, randomly paired test query's embedding. This is the arm that separates the two things A_fix confounds - loss of query conditioning versus loss of any per-instance variation in the injected block - and it is the first thing a reviewer will demand of a paper whose thesis is 'query conditioning does nothing'. The listed 'shuffled-bank retrieval sanity check' is described as a check that the retriever functions, not as this control, and A_rand is a fixed subset (no per-instance variation), so neither substitutes. Also absent: a retrieval upper bound (oracle item selection) to rule out 'weak retriever' as the explanation of a null, a diversified frozen subset (A_fix-MMR), and the plain long-context arm - the whole bank stuffed verbatim at N=100 - which is the natural RAG-vs-long-context comparator the proposal invokes in Related Work item (7) but never runs, since A_comp is a frontier-compiled summary instead.
preprint_collision: Above the median for this kind of check, and I credit it: it quotes text rather than gesturing, explicitly withdraws five arXiv IDs an earlier draft leaned on, reinstates one that the current search did return, concedes that 2602.02751 scoops the bank-size saturation claim outright, and concedes 2511.21730 as a partial collision on direction. It also adopts the search's own verdict that the direction is converging across 2025-2026 work - which is a real finding against the proposal's novelty, and the honest concession does not undo the deduction. Two substantive weaknesses. First, the author's standing rule ('nothing enters the novelty argument unless it appears in a search result I can quote') makes the check self-limiting: entire adjacent literatures that were not returned - in-context demonstration selection, adaptive/necessity-of-retrieval prediction, retrieval-vs-long-context - are excluded by construction, and only the last gets a paragraph in Related Work rather than a collision entry. That is exactly where I would expect the fatal precedent for 'fixed exemplars tie retrieved exemplars' to sit. Second, the disclosed history of fabricated IDs in a prior draft leaves residual verification risk on the load-bearing 2026 citations I cannot check here (2606.29824, 2602.02751, 2606.23127, 2607.01480, 2605.20616); if 2606.29824's pool-interference result exists as quoted, the mechanistic novelty reduces to a single MMR cell, and if it does not, the paper's designated rival account is unsourced. The admitted gap (no OpenReview 2026 sweep, and a 'freeze the retrieved subset' ablation plausibly living in some combined-system appendix) is the right residual risk to flag. Net: no outright collision named, but the check itself establishes that only the diagnostic and the volume-sign reinterpretation are novel, and both are the parts I judge weakest above.
